tagline.text: A hidden waterfall in inland Mindoro, reached by carabao cart across the river

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Ibuye, Calsapa (San Teodoro boundary), inland south of Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱700–2,000 (per person, cart, entrance and guide included, transport shared)

children.text: Tukuran Falls is a two-tier waterfall tucked into the hills inland and south of Puerto Galera, reached by a carabao-drawn cart that crosses shallow streams. It adds countryside scenery and creek swimming to a beach-focused Puerto Galera trip.

Tukuran Falls lies in the inland hills south of Puerto Galera in Oriental Mindoro. Tourism sites and travel blogs mostly present it as a Puerto Galera waterfall, but many sources give the village address as Sitio Ibuye, Barangay Calsapa, San Teodoro. The falls sit in hill country close to the boundary of the two municipalities, so sources disagree on which one it belongs to, and it is safest to find it on a map app by name and coordinates. Two maps place it at roughly 13.4336° N, 120.974° E.

The name is said to come from the local word for the rocks around the falls. The falls are described as two tiers: the first is narrow and drops into deep water, while the second spreads out wide and shallow like a fan. One blog puts the height at about
3m

, so think of it less as a grand waterfall and more as a creek playground where you can sit in clear water. Deeper, wider pools lie downstream, away from the noise of the cascade, and are said to be good for a quiet swim.

The journey is the character of this place. From the starting point, which works like a trailhead car park, you travel along a dirt track lined with coconut trees and across shallow streams, and you do it in a cart pulled by a carabao (water buffalo). Locals reportedly call the cart a kartel. The cart stops where you have to scramble over boulders, and from there the falls are only a few minutes on foot. If you prefer to walk, you can trek with a guide, crossing the stream, for about
30 minutes
The
White Beach

area of Puerto Galera is centered on parties and diving, but a half-day trip to Tukuran Falls takes you away from the beach to see countryside villages and a creek. Some visitors say the falls are small compared with others, so it suits people who enjoy the cart ride and the swimming themselves. One thing to know before you go: ratings are around 4.4 on Google Maps and 4.2 on Tripadvisor, and reviews generally praise the clear water, the fun cart ride and the friendly locals. On the other hand, some complain that certain guides inflate prices or push souvenirs. Information on fees also conflicts, with a regional tourism site listing free entry while blog posts mention separate entrance and environmental fees, so confirm current prices on site. Conditions at the stream crossings can change after rain, so check the previous day's weather too.
You ride a buffalo cart along the track between fields and coconut trees and cross knee-deep streams. A cart is said to carry up to
5 people
, and after it stops you have to climb the boulder section on foot.
A narrow, deep upper tier is followed by a wide, shallow lower tier. Many visitors say that sitting under the stream feels like a natural massage.
The pool below the falls is often described as clear and cold. Life vests can reportedly be rented, so even weaker swimmers can enjoy the shallow side.
Some people are known to jump from the rocks in the lowest section. The rocks can be slippery and sharp, so check the depth and follow the advice of your local guide.
If you walk instead of taking the cart, you cover about
1.5km
and cross the stream several times. A local guide usually goes with you, and shoes that can get wet are a must.

Tables, chairs and a simple shop are said to be near the falls. Reviews often mention local residents acting as guides and cooks, and some visitors eat grilled fish on site. However, there are no fixed menus or prices there, so check in advance.

blocks.title: A break from the beach party scene

children.text: Unlike the busy areas of Puerto Galera, the atmosphere is quiet and rural. It is a good choice if you want to swap one beach day for a creek and forest.
Set out from your accommodation, such as White Beach, by tricycle or multicab. The ride is said to take about
1 hour
Arrive at the starting point, pay the entrance and environmental fees and choose a guide. Checking the cart and guide fees in advance helps avoid disputes.
Ride the carabao cart past coconut trees and across streams for about
30 minutes
. Those who walk take about the same time.
Get off at the boulder section and walk a few minutes to the falls. Stand under the upper stream and swim in the pool below.
Rest over lunch prepared by local residents or snacks you brought yourself.
Ride the cart back to the starting point and head to Puerto Galera. Hurry so that you arrive before dark.
Many reviews say the falls are quiet early in the day. Tour groups can crowd the site in the afternoon, so a morning start is recommended.
Leave Puerto Galera by tricycle and agree on a route that passes the Tamaraw Falls area on the way.
Enjoy the cart ride and swimming at Tukuran Falls.
Have a late lunch at a nearby beach on the way back.
One blog review said Tukuran is far from other attractions, making it hard to combine several sites in one go. Agree on the plan with your local driver beforehand.

items.title: Two days, one night
items.subtitle: Puerto Galera beach and the falls

children.text: Leave Manila and take a ferry from Batangas Port to Puerto Galera.
Check in at White Beach or a nearby beach and enjoy the shore. This is also the time to ask about guides and fees for the next day's falls trip.
Leave early and finish the cart ride and swim at Tukuran Falls.
Return to Puerto Galera, have lunch, and head to the port in time for your ferry.
Return ferry times vary by season and operator, so check a later schedule to allow some slack if the falls trip runs long.
The usual route is a bus or van from Manila to Batangas Port, then a ferry to Puerto Galera. Allow close to half a day for the land and sea legs together.
Ferry schedules and fares vary by operator and season, so confirm them locally.
Arrivals in Puerto Galera may require online registration and proof of an accommodation booking. Check the latest notice.

items.title: From Calapan and the San Teodoro direction

children.text: Reviews describe taking a jeepney from Calapan toward Puerto Galera, getting off at the San Teodoro junction and then taking a tricycle to the starting point.
Bus and jeepney fares need to be checked for the latest prices. Tell the driver you are going to Tukuran Falls and he will tell you where to get off.

From November to May there is less rain, so the streams are easier to cross and the water tends to be clear. Because you cross the stream many times, heavy rain can swell the water, stopping the carts or restricting access.
Operating hours differ between sources, and some sites say daily from 7 AM to 7 PM, but I could not confirm this officially. Many reviews say early morning is the quietest.

Reviews say tour groups on weekends and holidays can make the wait for a cart long. A weekday morning is best, and once your plans are set, contact your guide the day before to ask whether a cart is available. The weather here changes often, so a raincoat and waterproof bag help all year round.

and may vary with local conditions.
Most travelers stay at White Beach or around Sabang in Puerto Galera, or in Calapan, and visit as a day trip. It is safest to assume there is no accommodation near the falls.

Tables, chairs and a simple drink and snack shop are said to be next to the falls. Reviews say local residents act as guides and cooks, but menus and prices must be confirmed on site. Bring cold water, snacks and a bag for your trash.

In Puerto Galera there are many bungalows and resorts, so booking is easy, while in Calapan you can choose a city hotel. For meals you can use the cooking offered by residents at the falls, or eat at restaurants in Puerto Galera town or on the beach on your way back. Seafood prices and menus differ between places, so ask the price before you order. Because the falls trip centers on the morning, a hearty breakfast and lunch on site works well.
Agree on the cart and guide fees before you set out, and haggle. Some reviews say a few guides ask for excessive fees.
Wear sandals or water shoes that can get wet. The dirt trail and rocks are slippery.
Bring a waterproof bag, a change of clothes and a towel. You cross the stream many times.
Go early in the morning for quiet. Tour groups can crowd the site in the afternoon.
If you want a local meal such as grilled fish, tell your guide beforehand.
Some guides encourage you to buy souvenirs, so politely decline if you do not need any.
Cart, entrance and guide fees are often paid in cash on site, so bring plenty of small bills and change.
Take your trash back with you and do not damage nature.
The stream can swell dangerously after rain. If the weather is bad, postpone the trip, and wear a life vest when swimming.
The boulder section and the place where you get off the cart are slippery. Water shoes are better than flip-flops.
Only jump from the rocks after checking the depth and the shape of the rocks yourself, and if you are unsure, do not jump.
Municipal affiliation and entrance fee rules differ between sources, so check the latest notice before visiting.
Beware of unofficial guides who approach you, and agree on the fee first.
The route is unclear for solo trekking, so go with a guide.
Guides and cart drivers are mostly village residents, so negotiate politely and keep to the price you agree on.
The starting base for the falls, about
1 hour
away by tricycle.
A beach where many tours are booked, with accommodation and restaurants clustered along it.
Known as a waterfall passed on the way from Puerto Galera, and it appears in review itineraries together with Tukuran.
A nearby attraction around Puerto Galera that also shows up in map apps.
